standard_prerequisites.name: Conditions, extensions and split pairs of the SADS forcing
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a linear order of order type omega plus omega* and a model with no solution, the elements split into the set U of those with finitely many predecessors and the set V of those with finitely many successors; a condition is a pair of a finite ascending sequence inside U and a finite descending sequence inside V, ordered by extension of both components, and a split pair is a pair whose ascending part lies entirely below its descending part; the author's own account is retained at source lines 1112, 1114 and 1117-1119.
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes all the objects of the counted lemma, and in particular the observation that a split pair has one component inside U or inside V, which is what makes the first case of the proof work.

standard_prerequisites.name: The two forcing relations and the forcing question
standard_prerequisites.statement: A condition forces convergence on side i when the corresponding finite string already converges, and forces divergence on side i when no compatible split pair extension converges there; the forcing question between the two sides holds when some split pair extending the condition makes both designated computations converge; the author's own definitions are retained at source lines 1121-1127 and 1143-1145.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is exactly the statement that this forcing question is decided on a non-empty condition, with the two cases producing extensions forcing convergence or divergence on one side.

core_obligations: First case: assume the forcing question holds. Then, using Y, find a split pair extending the condition on which both designated computations converge, and use that a split pair has one component inside U or inside V, which is decided Y-prime computably, to obtain an extension forcing convergence on the corresponding side (source line 1159).

Second case: assume the forcing question fails. Search through the finite ascending sequences above the first component and below the second, and enumerate the values of their maximum whenever a new smaller such value appears, obtaining a Y-computable descending sequence which by hypothesis must be finite (source line 1161).

Conclude that either nothing is enumerated, in which case the condition already forces divergence on the first side and one is done, or a minimal such sequence exists and can be found Y-prime computably (source line 1161).
Symmetrically, either the condition already forces divergence on the second side or a maximal descending sequence can be found Y-prime computably (source line 1163).

In the remaining case use the failure of the forcing question to rule out that both found sequences lie inside U respectively V, decide Y-prime computably which of the two inclusions fails, and extend the condition by that element to get divergence on the corresponding side, verified through the minimality that was arranged (source line 1165).

proof_roadmap.step: Case of a successful forcing question: take a split pair and read off convergence on one side.

Case of a failing forcing question: enumerate candidates below the second component and above the first, and use the absence of a solution plus minimality/maximality to find the witnesses Y-prime computably.
Rule out both witnesses lying on the wrong sides, extend by one element and verify the forced divergence.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2402.11616v3 的 Lemma lem:sads-forcing-question-sigma01（源 1149-1156 行，证明 1158-1166 行）：在 SADS 的 split-pair 力迫下，forcing question 成立与否两种情况都能 Y′-可计算地判出，并各自给出扩展使某一侧强制收敛或发散。关键操作不是例行核验：第一种情况必须用「split pair 的两半必有一半落在 U 或 V 内」这一核心性质把收敛搬到某一侧（1159 行）；第二种情况要造一个 Y-可计算的下降序列枚举、利用「模型内不存在解」假设断定它有限，再用最小/最大性把见证找出来并判定属于哪一侧（1161-1163 行），最后用 forcing question 失败排除两个见证同时落在正确侧，再补一个元素得到发散（1165 行）。难点在于两种情况的对称处理与「用最小性保证发散」的验证；原文位置在证明的 1159、1161-1163 与 1165 行。
